record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: How can billiard models be generalized to include more realistic physical effects, such as soft wall potentials, external fields, dissipative or stochastic scattering at the boundary or in the interior, and time-dependent boundaries, while retaining mathematical or physical interest as models of open dynamical systems?

evidence.quote: Open problem 16. Generalisations: Billiards with more realistic physical effects, for example soft wall potentials, external fields, dissipative and/or stochastic scattering (at the boundary or in the interior) or time dependent boundaries.
The possibilities are endless; for this reason, it is increasingly important to carefully justify the mathematical and/or physical interest of any new model.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An open billiard is a dynamical system in which a point particle moves freely inside a region $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ (or on a Riemannian manifold) with piecewise smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$, undergoing specular reflection (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) whenever it hits $\partial\Omega$, and where some portion of the boundary is removed (a "hole") so that trajectories can escape. The escape dynamics gives rise to questions about survival probabilities, conditionally invariant measures, escape rates, and fractal repellers.

Develop mathematically rigorous generalizations of the open billiard framework that incorporate one or more of the following physically realistic features, while preserving enough structure to study escape rates, invariant or conditionally invariant measures, and statistical properties:

(a) Soft-wall potentials: replace the hard-wall reflection by Hamiltonian motion in a smooth confining potential $V:\mathbb{R}^d 	o \mathbb{R}$ that approximates the indicator of $\Omega$ as a stiffness parameter tends to infinity, and analyze the dynamics for finite stiffness.

(b) External fields: include a smooth external force (for example a constant gravitational field, a magnetic field giving rise to Larmor circular arcs, or a general potential force) acting on the particle between collisions.

(c) Dissipative or stochastic scattering: replace specular reflection by a dissipative reflection law (with a fixed or velocity-dependent restitution coefficient) and/or by a stochastic reflection law in which the post-collision direction is drawn from a prescribed kernel (for instance the Maxwell–Boltzmann or cosine law); allow analogous stochastic perturbations of the interior dynamics.

(d) Time-dependent boundaries: allow $\partial\Omega = \partial\Omega_t$ to vary with time according to a prescribed (possibly periodic or random) law, and study the resulting non-autonomous open system, including phenomena such as Fermi acceleration.

In each case, formulate precise definitions of the model, identify natural classes of examples (such as Sinai, Bunimovich, or Lorentz-type geometries with holes), and establish results on existence and properties of invariant or quasi-stationary measures, escape rates, ergodic and mixing properties, and the limit behaviour as the perturbation parameters tend to the idealized hard-wall, conservative, deterministic, or static cases.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad research programme rather than a single sharply posed conjecture. Substantial work has appeared on individual aspects (soft-potential limits to billiards by Baladi–Demers and others, magnetic and gravitational billiards, stochastic and Maxwell-type boundary scattering in kinetic theory, dissipative billiards by De Simoi, Del Magno and collaborators, time-dependent billiards and Fermi acceleration by Pereira, Turaev, Gelfreich, etc.), but no comprehensive theory unifying these realistic generalizations of open billiards exists. The overall problem remains open as a research direction.

status_evidence.title: Open billiards survey (zbMATH entry)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists generalisations involving soft wall potentials, external fields, dissipative/stochastic scattering, and time-dependent boundaries as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Dissipative billiards and SRB measures
status_evidence.snippet: Studies billiards with contracting reflection laws as dissipative generalizations.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for dissipative reflection laws but not in a unified open-billiard framework.

status_evidence.title: Fermi acceleration in time-dependent billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes time-dependent billiard boundaries and unbounded energy growth.
status_evidence.claim: Time-dependent boundary models have been studied but many questions remain open.
